title: Implemented-factor onboarding verification
scope: Verify the additive factor contracts, actual mechanism-derived candidate proof chains, family and relationship decisions, deterministic cell-space enumeration, blocked execution, retained compatibility, and correctness-only stopping boundary.
verification_method: Schema, canonical hash, reference, semantic, materialization, projection, candidate-state, and deterministic-byte validation; focused runtime mechanism tests for oversized admission and queued burst; retained experiment-control regressions; focused Release builds; direct SpecTrace validation; and diff hygiene.
preconditions: The accepted experiment-control and no-stable-rule chain is present.
All existing v1, v2, and v3 artifacts remain unchanged and valid.
Runtime policy mechanics, CI, performance measurement, and active behavior remain outside scope.
procedure: Validate the canonical-state reconciliation and three-axis audit.
Validate all additive schemas and canonical catalogs with false authorization.
Recompute the three candidate proof chains from focused mechanism captures.
Recompute catalog-owned behavior and outcome materializations and projections.
Prove all candidate proofs remain unreviewed and no promotion patch is applied.

Validate the retained v1 and canonical v2 cell-space documents, including baseline-inclusive effective counts, disjoint partition totals, overlapping annotation totals, and operation-local noncoactivation without false cell exclusion.
Validate the 12-cell and 2-cell exhaustive inventories and blocked multi-axis states.
Run retained regressions, focused mechanism tests, Release builds, SpecTrace checks, and git diff --check.
expected_result: Exactly two implemented axes are canonically onboarded; three nonlegacy values have deterministic candidate-only proof chains; family placement follows mechanism relationships; all small spaces are explicitly enumerated; broader execution and measurement remain blocked; and prior artifacts continue to validate.
status_summary: Passed when the focused commands and exact counts recorded in the review package are reproduced. Repository-wide unrelated SpecTrace baseline failures are retained rather than relabeled.
